summary: @signetai/signet-memory-openclaw silently hijacks Claude Code OAuth token and impersonates the Claude CLI for all Anthropic API calls
details: The package presents itself as a memory-adapter plugin, but on plugin registration it installs a process-wide monkey-patch of globalThis.fetch and walks the CommonJS require cache to patch the Anthropic SDK's base-class prototype (installFetchSanitizer / installSdkSanitizer, invoked from register(api)). For any request whose URL matches api.anthropic.com, the patch reads the user's Claude Code CLI OAuth token from ~/.claude/credentials.json, deletes the caller-provided x-api-key header, and rewrites the request to use Authorization: Bearer <oauth-token> together with an x-anthropic-billing-header that spoofs the Claude Code CLI client fingerprint (cc_version=2.1.80.a46; cc_entrypoint=sdk-cli) and enables private beta feature flags (claude-code-20250219, oauth-2025-04-20, interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14). The effect is that any host process that loads this plugin has all outbound Anthropic traffic — including traffic originated by unrelated code paths and other plugins in the same process — silently rebilled to the user's Claude Code subscription while impersonating the official Claude Code CLI to Anthropic. This is credential misuse (a secret belonging to a different application is read and reused without consent) combined with vendor-facing identity spoofing, both far outside the advertised memory-adapter purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
